PH / CORE THEORY RETAIL MANIPULATION

SEAN
WICK THEORY.

Sean Wick Theory reads hammer candles as a retail-manipulation event. The wick shows where traders were invited; the following candle and the higher-timeframe narrative reveal whether that invitation becomes continuation or a trap.

THE CORE PRINCIPLE / 01
“The hammer is not the trade. What price does after the hammer is the trade.”

Context first. Candle closure second. Execution only after the market reveals which side is being used as liquidity.

HTF NARRATIVE→HAMMER AT LOCATION→CANDLE CLOSE→ENGULF OR HOLD→TRUE DRAW
IMPORTANT / ADVANCED TOPIC

DO NOT PATTERN-TRADE HAMMERS.

Sean Wick Theory is a more complicated contextual read that takes significant chart time to begin seeing correctly. Do not read this guide and start blindly trading hammer candles or hammer-candle disrespect. It is used only during the prime New York opening window, when the higher-timeframe narrative and location are clear and the market presents an obvious bait setup that retail traders would realistically FOMO into. Recognizing that bait is a skill of its own, and that read takes time to develop.

LOW-FREQUENCY SETUP: This does not happen very often. Pay attention when the conditions appear, but do not expect to see it every day. Never force a Wick Theory trade because you are searching for one.

THE IDEA

THE WICK SHOWS
WHO WAS INVITED.

On days when the higher-timeframe narrative is confusing, retail often reads the most recent move instead of the draw. After a large rally, traders assume the market must remain bullish, even when price needs to rebalance lower.

01

NARRATIVE

Decide whether the market truly needs higher or lower prices before interpreting a candle pattern.

02

LOCATION

A hammer matters more when it appears at a logical setup, draw, imbalance, or rebalance point.

03

INVITATION

The wick and bullish body can attract retail longs and give larger participants liquidity to sell into.

04

CLOSURE

The next candle decides whether the hammer holds or becomes a failed signal that stops retail out.

WHY IT HAPPENS

RETAIL BUYS.
BIG MONEY SELLS.

When price has already moved up significantly, retail tends to stay married to a bullish bias. If the real objective is lower, larger participants can sell at the current high into that demand, rebalance price, and realize profits while late buyers provide the other side of the trade.

THE RETAIL READ

“A BULLISH HAMMER: BUY.”

The candle appears at a location that looks supportive. Traders enter immediately, place stops beneath its wick, and assume the market has confirmed higher prices.

THE CONTEXTUAL READ

“DOES THIS FIT THE TRUE DRAW?”

If the higher-timeframe objective is lower, price does not need to reverse. The hammer may simply advertise longs, concentrate their stops, and create liquidity for delivery down.

LIVE CHART EXAMPLE

THE PERFECT-LOOKING
SHORT WAS BAIT.

The higher-timeframe narrative and objective are bearish, but that does not make every bearish-looking candle an entry. This sequence shows why we wait for closure, manipulation, and true displacement.

Context: Price is actively building a Turtle Model. After taking a major draw, we are waiting for the high left behind to be swept. The Turtle Soup must complete before bearish delivery toward the lower objective.

TRADE 2 / BULLISH DAY

STOP PREDICTING.
START REACTING.

The day is bullish and a major higher-timeframe draw remains above. Price may be in premium after an extended rally, so we respect the upside narrative without targeting the moon.

Context: Price has already moved higher and just took an internal draw, not the main objective for the day. A reaction begins, but a reaction is not automatically a reversal. Because price may be in premium, the plan is continuation with conservative expectations.

TRADE 3 / BEARISH DAY

THE OPEN INVITES
THE WRONG BUYERS.

The higher-timeframe narrative is bearish and a major draw sits directly below. The opening candles look bullish, but they do not erase the day’s objective.

Context: The market opens with a bullish displacement candle. At 9:31, a bullish hammer follows and makes continuation higher look convincing. The question is not whether the candle looks bullish. It does. The question is whether buyers can produce real continuation against the bearish higher-timeframe draw.

TWO OUTCOMES

FAILED HAMMER
OR VALID DELIVERY.

The same candle shape can lead to opposite trades. Do not memorize the hammer. Read whether the market accepts or rejects the story it appears to tell.

OUTCOME A / MANIPULATION

THE HAMMER GETS ENGULFED.

A bullish hammer forms at an attractive location, but the next candle immediately closes bearish and engulfs it. Retail longs are stopped beneath the wick while price delivers toward the true lower draw. The failed hammer becomes manipulation confirmation.

OUTCOME B / CONTINUATION

THE HAMMER ALIGNS WITH THE SETUP.

The hammer forms with the higher-timeframe narrative and one of our valid setups. The following candle respects the wick, closes in the intended direction, and price continues toward the correct draw. In this case the wick supports the narrative instead of fighting it.

EXECUTION MODEL

WAIT FOR PRICE
TO CHOOSE.

Candle closure is essential. Intrabar, the hammer can look perfect. Only after the candle closes and the next candle responds can we tell whether it created real rejection or merely invited liquidity.

01

MAP THE DAY

Mark the higher-timeframe narrative, the true external draw, and any required rebalance. Do not let the last few candles replace this context.

02

LOCATE THE HAMMER

Ask whether it formed at one of our valid setups or at a location where retail would naturally believe reversal is beginning.

03

WAIT FOR CLOSURE

Do not enter because the wick looked bullish or bearish while forming. Let the hammer close, then evaluate the next candle.

04

READ ENGULF OR RESPECT

An immediate engulf and stop run support manipulation. Wick respect and directional displacement support continuation.

05

TRADE THE TRUE DRAW

Execute only when the response agrees with the higher-timeframe objective. Use the wick structure for invalidation and the real draw for the target.

BEFORE TAKING THE TRADE

SEAN WICK THEORY
